title: Pin git output formatting for exact-match history checks
context: pathKnownToHistory uses exact string matching against git log output as a safety guard against directory/glob pathname bypasses. Round 5 introduced this check, Round 6 review found it creates false positives when git's default output formatting diverges from raw input: core.quotePath defaults true (non-ASCII paths get backslash-octal-quoted), and --name-only with default diff simplification omits merge commits entirely. Both cause legitimate file deletions to appear never-tracked, triggering the guard's own "retry with cwd" advice and misrouting writes to wrong worktree—reproducing issue #54 through this function's fix.
decision: Explicitly control git output formatting for string-equality comparisons by adding -c core.quotePath=false and --diff-merges=first-parent. This restores output format to match raw input, enabling reliable exact-string matching. Both flags follow existing convention elsewhere in the file (commitFiles uses core.quotePath=false for the same reason).
consequences: False positives eliminated: non-ASCII filenames and merge-resolved deletions correctly recognized as known-to-history
Guard prevents legitimate deletes being misrouted to wrong worktrees, fully closing issue #54
Two regression tests added to catch this failure mode in future reviews
Pattern established: git output normalization must be explicitly controlled in safety-critical string comparisons
alternatives_rejected: Normalize the path string after retrieval (less reliable, adds complexity, fragile to future git default changes)
Apply only core.quotePath=false without --diff-merges=first-parent (incomplete, leaves merge-commit false positives unfixed)
Document the limitation as an acceptable tradeoff (false positives are severe; obeying the guard causes data misrouting)
